topic: 限时写作：图表概述与关键比较 · Independent new scenario: technology assessment and hidden assumptions
grammarFocus: 趋势、比较、比例、时态与数据句的准确性。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Campus Shuttle App: A Tech Assessment with Hidden Assumptions
instructions: 本材料为项目原创模拟场景、人物与数据，不是官方雅思试题，也未经考生难度标定。先听分角色美式合成录音，再答10题；留意说话人的更正、条件和立场。录音未重做前不可把旧音频配给本稿。所有题干与选项为英文，解析为中文。填空按题目词数和原文词形作答。语法先学习规则，再完成8项独立新句或新数据练习。口语与写作迁移另用自己的新细节；完成本练习不等于独立能力已达标。
transcript:
Maya: Hi, everyone. Thanks for coming to the student technology committee meeting. I'm Maya, and I run the committee this term. We're here to talk about the new campus shuttle app. The pilot starts next Monday, and we need to decide what to recommend to the university. Let's start with the data from last month's survey. Ben, can you give us the numbers?

Ben: Sure. We asked 400 students about the old shuttle system. Only 28 percent said they were satisfied with the current app. That's a big problem. But when we asked about the new app, 65 percent said they would probably use it. That's a huge jump.

Maya: Wait, Ben, let me check that. You said 65 percent would probably use it? I thought the number was 56 percent.

Ben: Oh, you're right. Sorry, I mixed up two surveys. The 65 percent was for the library app. For the shuttle app, it's 56 percent. So, 56 percent said they would probably use the new shuttle app.

Maya: Thanks for correcting that. Fifty-six is twice twenty-eight, but that doesn't mean satisfaction has doubled. One answer reports current satisfaction; the other predicts possible use. We must keep those measures separate. What about the cost?

Ben: The new app costs $12,000 to develop. The old app costs $8,000 a year to maintain. The new app will cost $5,000 a year to maintain. So, in the first year, the total cost is $17,000. After that, it's $5,000 a year. The old app is $8,000 every year. So, the new app saves money after about two years.

Maya: Hold on. The yearly maintenance saving is only three thousand dollars. It takes four years to recover the twelve-thousand-dollar development cost. At the end of year four, each option totals thirty-two thousand, assuming these costs stay unchanged.

Ben: You're right. Lower annual maintenance is not the same as a lower total cost immediately. From year five, the new app would be cheaper overall, unless extra costs arose.

Maya: Now, let's talk about the hidden assumptions. Some students assume the new app will work everywhere on campus. But the pilot only covers the main campus. The north campus is not included yet. That's an important limitation.

Ben: Right. Also, some people think the app will show real-time bus locations. But in the pilot, it only shows scheduled times. Real-time tracking comes later, maybe next year.

Maya: So, we need to be careful about what we promise. The survey shows interest, but the pilot is limited. Let's recommend the pilot, but with clear information about these limits. Any questions?

Ben: One more thing. The survey also asked about the old app's problems. The top problem was that it often crashed. 45 percent of students said it crashed at least once a week. The new app is designed to crash less, but we don't have data yet.

Maya: During the pilot, let's record failures per one hundred attempted checks, not just total complaints. If twice as many people try the app, the number of complaints could rise even when the failure rate falls.

Ben: And we should compare the same routes and times of day. Otherwise a quieter service could make the app seem more reliable. We can report the limits alongside the results.

Maya: Okay. So, our recommendation: support the pilot, but tell students about the limited coverage and the scheduled times only. And we should collect data during the pilot. Does everyone agree?

Ben: Yes, I agree.

Maya: Great. Let's meet again in two weeks to review the first pilot data. Thanks, everyone.

questions.prompt: What is the corrected percentage for probable shuttle-app use?
questions.explanation: 65%来自图书馆应用调查；Ben更正校车应用为56%。28%是现有应用满意度，45%是每周崩溃报告比例。
questions.evidence: For the shuttle app, it's 56 percent. So, 56 percent said they would probably use the new shuttle app.

questions.prompt: Why does Maya keep the two survey measures separate?
options: Both surveys measure the same kind of current satisfaction.
Possible future use and current satisfaction are different measures.
The figures show that satisfaction has already doubled.
The figures describe only the app's development cost.
answers: Possible future use and current satisfaction are different measures.
questions.explanation: 一个问题问现有满意度，另一个问可能使用意向；56是28的两倍，但这不是满意度翻倍的证据。
questions.evidence: Fifty-six is twice twenty-eight, but that doesn't mean satisfaction has doubled. One answer reports current satisfaction; the other predicts possible use.

questions.prompt: What is the new app's first-year total cost?
questions.explanation: 第一年开发12,000加维护5,000，共17,000；12,000只计开发，8,000是旧应用一年维护费。
questions.evidence: So, in the first year, the total cost is $17,000.

questions.prompt: According to the corrected calculation, when are the two cumulative costs equal if the stated costs stay unchanged?
options: At the end of year two
At the end of year four
At the start of year one
At the end of year five
answers: At the end of year four
questions.explanation: 旧应用8,000×4=32,000；新应用12,000+5,000×4=32,000。Ben早先的两年说法被更正，不能作为最终答案。
questions.evidence: At the end of year four, each option totals thirty-two thousand, assuming these costs stay unchanged.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE WORD from the transcript: The ______ campus is not included in the pilot.
questions.explanation: 试点只覆盖主校区，north campus尚未纳入。
questions.evidence: But the pilot only covers the main campus. The north campus is not included yet.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE WORD from the transcript: In the pilot, passengers see ______ times rather than live bus locations.
questions.explanation: 试点只显示scheduled times；实时追踪是以后可能加入的功能。
questions.evidence: But in the pilot, it only shows scheduled times.

questions.prompt: What was the main reported problem with the old app?
options: No access to library opening hours
questions.explanation: Ben说旧应用的首要问题是经常崩溃；费用和图书馆信息属于其他信息，不能混用。
questions.evidence: The top problem was that it often crashed. 45 percent of students said it crashed at least once a week.

questions.prompt: The committee already has measurements showing that the new app crashes less.
questions.explanation: 设计目标是更少崩溃，但明确说还没有数据，直接反驳已经有测量证明。
questions.evidence: The new app is designed to crash less, but we don't have data yet.

questions.prompt: Why record failures per hundred checks instead of only counting complaints?
options: The amount of use may change, so totals alone can be misleading.
Every complaint always represents exactly one hundred failures.
The committee no longer needs to record attempted checks.
A higher complaint count proves that the failure rate increased.
answers: The amount of use may change, so totals alone can be misleading.
questions.explanation: 使用量增加时，即使故障率下降，投诉总量也可能上升。按检查次数作分母才能区分总量和率；仍须保留方法限制。
questions.evidence: During the pilot, let's record failures per one hundred attempted checks, not just total complaints. If twice as many people try the app, the number of complaints could rise even when the failure rate falls.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE WORD from the transcript: The committee will review the first pilot data in ______ weeks.
questions.explanation: 最后约定两周后再会，看的是首批试点数据；next Monday是开始试点的日期。
questions.evidence: Let's meet again in two weeks to review the first pilot data.

vocabulary.example: The pilot starts next Monday, and we need to decide what to recommend to the university.
Only 28 percent said they were satisfied with the current app.
The old app costs $8,000 a year to maintain.
Maya: Now, let's talk about the hidden assumptions.
So, our recommendation: support the pilot, but tell students about the limited coverage and the scheduled times only.
The new app is designed to crash less, but we don't have data yet.
The pilot starts next Monday, and we need to decide what to recommend to the university.

grammar.title: 准确描述比例、变化与比较；保留数据限制
grammar.explanation: 复习过去时及比较级。本课新增：percent表示以原数为分母的比例变化，percentage points表示两个百分比直接相减；同样人数在不同分母中可能代表不同的比例。the number通常按单数，percent of后的动词则要看实际对象，如equipment为不可数单数。比较相同指标时可用that替代单数名词短语，避免把旅程长短同城市直接比较。预测或早期意向不能写成已经证明的成效。也复习未来被动will be + 过去分词，明确它是结构复习而不是本课新比例规则。以下八题使用新情境或新数据。
grammar.example: One answer reports current satisfaction; the other predicts possible use.

questions.prompt: A share moved from 25% to 40%. Which statement is accurate?
questions.explanation: 40%-25%=15个百分点；相对增长15/25=60%，两种单位不能互换。
questions.evidence: The share increased by 15 percentage points, from 25% to 40%.

questions.prompt: Choose the past-tense form: The number of complaints ______ from 80 to 60 during last year's trial.
questions.explanation: last year指定结束的过去时间；fall的过去式是fell，不是fall的被动形式。
questions.evidence: The number of complaints fell from 80 to 60 during last year's trial.

questions.prompt: Of 200 respondents, 50 supported a proposal. Which proportion is correct?
questions.evidence: Twenty-five percent of the respondents supported the proposal.

questions.prompt: Twenty of 50 cyclists and twenty of 100 drivers reported delays. Which comparison is accurate?
options: The shares were equal because the counts were equal.
The share among cyclists was 20 percent.
The share among drivers was twice the share among cyclists.
The share among cyclists was twice the share among drivers.
answers: The share among cyclists was twice the share among drivers.
questions.explanation: 骑车者20/50=40%，驾车者20/100=20%；相同人数不代表相同比例。
questions.evidence: The share among cyclists was twice the share among drivers.

questions.prompt: Complete the present-tense statement: Thirty percent of the equipment ______ unavailable.
questions.explanation: 这里实际对象是不可数单数equipment，现在时用is。percent of后不能不看名词就一律用复数动词。
questions.evidence: Thirty percent of the equipment is unavailable.

questions.prompt: Keep the comparison parallel: The average journey in Town A was longer than ______.
questions.explanation: that替代单数the average journey；不能把旅程与城市或人直接比较，those是复数替代。
questions.evidence: The average journey in Town A was longer than that in Town B.

questions.prompt: A survey records plans to buy a ticket, not actual purchases. Which report stays within that evidence?
options: The survey confirms that all future customers are satisfied.
The survey suggests possible demand but does not establish actual sales.
The number of plans is identical to the number of completed sales.
The survey proves that every planned purchase has already occurred.
answers: The survey suggests possible demand but does not establish actual sales.
questions.explanation: 意向能提示潜在需求，不能当成已完成购买或满意度证据。The survey suggests possible demand but does not establish actual sales 保留了这一证据边界。
questions.evidence: The survey suggests possible demand but does not establish actual sales.

questions.prompt: Revision: choose the future passive form. The next survey ______ in November.
questions.explanation: survey是被开展的对象；未来被动为will be conducted。
questions.evidence: The next survey will be conducted in November.

part3: What are some common hidden assumptions people make about new technology?
How can schools or companies test new technology before using it widely?
Do you think the cost of technology is always worth the benefits?
How can data help people make better decisions about technology?

Write a short report (about 150 words) for the university about a pilot of a new campus food-ordering app. Include: the percentage of students interested, the cost, one hidden assumption, and your recommendation. Use accurate data sentences and clear comparisons.
